$comment: JJ-043: where both books have a drink, the IBA spec ships and the Savoy one does not.
Every Savoy recipe whose normalised name matches an IBA drink must appear in exactly one of the
two sections below; build_cocktails.py fails on a candidate it cannot find here. 'superseded'
names the IBA drink that replaces it; 'distinct' says why it is a different drink that happens to
share the name. Pairs the name match cannot see (a drink the books name differently) are listed
under 'superseded' by hand. Reviewed drink by drink, 2026-10-09, against both extractions.

alexander-cocktail-no-2.why: brandy, crème de cacao and cream in equal parts: the IBA Alexander

angel-face-cocktail.why: gin, apricot brandy and calvados in equal parts

aviation-cocktail.why: the same drink; the Savoy famously omits the crème de violette

brandy-crusta-cocktail.why: brandy, curaçao, maraschino, lemon and bitters

casino-cocktail.why: Old Tom gin, maraschino, orange bitters and lemon

clover-club-cocktail.why: gin, lemon, egg white and a red syrup; grenadine in 1930, raspberry today

corpse-reviver-no-2.why: gin, Cointreau, Lillet, lemon and a dash of absinthe

martini-dry-cocktail.why: two thirds gin, one third French vermouth: a Dry Martini under the book's other title

the-french-75-cocktail.why: gin, lemon and sugar topped with Champagne

john-collins.why: gin, lemon, sugar and soda; Hollands in 1930

manhattan-cocktail-sweet.why: whisky and Italian vermouth: the Manhattan itself, the 'sweet' only setting it against the dry one

martinez-cocktail.why: gin, vermouth, maraschino and orange bitters

monkey-gland-cocktail.why: gin, orange juice, absinthe and grenadine

paradise-cocktail.why: gin, apricot brandy and orange juice

sazerac-cocktail.why: the same drink; rye in 1930, cognac in the IBA spec

singapore-sling.why: the same name for the same drink; the IBA spec is the Raffles one

stinger-cocktail.why: brandy and white crème de menthe

tipperary-cocktail-no-1.why: Irish whiskey, Italian vermouth and green Chartreuse

tuxedo-cocktail-no-2.why: gin, French vermouth, maraschino, absinthe and orange bitters

southern-mint-julep.why: whisky, mint and sugar; named differently, found by hand

new-orleans-gin-fizz.why: gin, citrus, sugar, egg white, cream and orange-flower water: the Ramos Gin Fizz, found by hand

distinct.alexander-cocktail-no-1: gin, not brandy: the original gin Alexander
distinct.corpse-reviver-no-1: brandy, calvados and Italian vermouth; nothing in common with the No. 2
distinct.manhattan-cocktail-dry: French and Italian vermouth together: the drink now called a Perfect Manhattan
distinct.manhattan-cocktail-no-1: the nineteenth-century build, with curaçao or maraschino and a wineglass of vermouth
distinct.tipperary-cocktail-no-2: gin, French vermouth, orange juice, grenadine and mint: another drink under the same name
distinct.tuxedo-cocktail-no-1: no maraschino and no bitters; gin, French vermouth, absinthe and lemon peel
